pr.title: perf(prim_ts) keep D512 grouped Keeps for decode planned at a long max_kv_len
pr.body:
## 📌 Description

#9771 selects grouped Keeps Q64 for D512 GQA8 decode with NVFP4 KV at q_len > 1. That selection doesn't hold at every batch size and plan length. When the Keeps grid doesn't fill a wave, `_resolve_grouped_q_launch_candidates` limits Keeps to one wave of splits (`multi_wave and (fills_wave or sm107_smem_transform)`). Swaps Q64 can use up to 8 waves. Wherever the extra splits lower its modeled time, Swaps Q64 wins.

This happens at some batch sizes with short plans: for example B13 with 32 Q / 4 KV heads at `max_kv_len` 8192 or 32768 picks `Sq64g8/s5`. It happens at most batch sizes up to 32 once the plan is long. Engines such as vLLM plan decode once at startup with `max_kv_len` set to the model context (e.g. 262144) and capture the plan in CUDA graphs, so they hit the Swaps path.

For D512, Keeps Q64 and Swaps Q64 score the same extra waves. This PR lets D512 Keeps keep its multi-wave split fanout (`or probe.headdim == 512`). The change set is exactly `Sq64g8/sN` → `Kq64g8/sN` with the same split count N; nothing else changes.

**Performance** (B200, clocks unlocked, D512, 32 Q / 4 KV heads, FP8 Q, NVFP4 KV, q_len 8 causal, plan `max_kv_len` 262144; µs, median over 6 processes, CUPTI timing):

| B | KV length | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1024 | 43.1 | 32.5 | 0.75 |
| 8 | 4096 | 62.9 | 47.2 | 0.75 |
| 8 | 16384 | 115.2 | 96.1 | 0.83 |
| 8 | 32768 (30720 shared prefix) | 174.2 | 135.9 | 0.78 |
| 8 | 131072 | 550.6 | 488.8 | 0.89 |
| 8 | 262144 | 1049.3 | 965.9 | 0.92 |
| 8 | half 8192, half 131072 | 383.6 | 312.3 | 0.81 |
| 32 | 16384 | 393.2 | 320.1 | 0.81 |
| 32 | 32768 | 634.4 | 549.6 | 0.87 |
| 32 | 262144 | 4749.1 | 4362.1 | 0.92 |

Short plans, same setup (each side is its tree's default selection; main `Sq64g8/sN`, this PR `Kq64g8/sN` with the same N):

| B | q_len | plan `max_kv_len` | KV length | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | 8 | 8192 | 8192 | 107.2 | 89.1 | 0.83 |
| 13 | 8 | 8192 | 2048 | 62.2 | 48.4 | 0.78 |
| 13 | 8 | 32768 | 32768 | 281.5 | 235.6 | 0.84 |
| 13 | 8 | 32768 | 4096 | 81.0 | 63.8 | 0.79 |
| 13 | 8 | 32768 | alternating 2048 / 32768 | 180.9 | 143.7 | 0.79 |
| 24 | 8 | 2048 | 2048 | 67.8 | 52.8 | 0.78 |
| 30 | 8 | 32768 | 32768 | 578.6 | 506.4 | 0.88 |
| 6 | 32 | 8192 | 8192 | 139.5 | 105.8 | 0.76 |

- **Long plans.** Across 348 + 24 + 40 + 18 timed points, the PR is 0.71–0.93x of main wherever the config changes, and never slower. These cover TP1/TP2 head splits, B 4–128, q_len 2–32 causal and dense, plans 40960–262144, and actual lengths 1K–256K. Points where main already selects Keeps keep the same config.
- **Short plans.** Across 35 timed points where the config changes, the PR is 0.75–0.88x of main, and every PR process was faster than every main process. These cover heads 32/4, 16/2 and 8/1; B 5–115; q_len 2–32 causal and dense; plans 2048–32768; uniform and mixed actual lengths.
- **Why not one-wave Keeps.** Forcing one-wave Keeps instead is faster than Swaps for uniform long batches. For mixed-length batches it is up to 1.41x slower than main, which is why the multi-wave split fanout is kept.
- **Correctness.** Every output was compared with an fp32 reference on the E4M3-rounded K/V. Min cosine 0.99982.

**Scope** (plan-only, mocked 148-SM SM100, FP8 Q, NVFP4 KV, every B from 1 to 256, heads 32/4, 16/2 and 8/1, q_len 1–32, causal and dense):

| plan `max_kv_len` | plans | changed |
|---|---|---|
| 2048–32768 | 294,912 | 14,160 (q_len 2–32, B 5–126) |
| 40960–262144 | 245,760 | 20,532 (q_len 2–32, B 2–131) |
| 2048–32768, page 16 and 128 | 46,080 | 2,720 |

- Every changed config is `Sq64g8/sN` → `Kq64g8/sN` with the same N. No Swaps Q64 config is left with this PR, and there were no errors on either tree.
- No change for q_len 1. FP8 KV and GQA16 or 64/4 heads don't change at any B (204,800 plans).
- At the changed long-plan timing points, the full plan config equals main's with Keeps forced.
